responses_archetypeVariants.sophisticate: The charge is methodological and deserves a methodological answer: the sophisticate says the antinatalist parades atrocities to misrepresent a distribution whose mass sits nowhere near the tails. Concede the mass. The average life is not bone cancer, and granting that costs nothing, because the argument was never about the average — it is about the object of a risk decision, and in every serious domain of risk ethics that object is the whole distribution, tails included. A regulator does not wave through a fatal adverse effect because most patients tolerate the drug; a safety board does not strike death from its analysis because most workers clock out alive. The tails are not rhetoric smuggled in to inflame. They are structural features of the outcome space that every act of procreation actually engages, because the parent cannot bind which ticket the child draws. To call their inclusion cherry-picking is to confuse a complete accounting of a gamble with a biased sample of a population — a category error, and one that cuts the other way: it is the optimist who is sampling, pricing the wager off the modal outcome while discounting the tail he cannot rule out for his own child. And the decisive move needs no tail at all. Strip the distribution to its guaranteed baseline — not catastrophe, only the certainties: aging, the loss of everyone loved, bodily decline, death — and that baseline already triggers the asymmetry, because it is suffering imposed on someone who never consented to receive it. You do not need leukemia to make the case. You need only the certainty that the created being will be made to undergo pain and loss it did not agree to, which the modal life delivers in full.
